intent: The question's own text, rendered as the legend of its QuestionnaireItem's fieldset.

dont_use_when.situation: A caption for a group of fields in an ordinary form

instead.note: A QuestionnaireTitle throws outside a QuestionnaireItem.

invariants.text: It renders a `<legend>`; the first legend child of the item's fieldset is that fieldset's caption and its accessible name.

anti_patterns.dont: Put the question in a heading or paragraph inside the item instead of QuestionnaireTitle
anti_patterns.do_instead: Use QuestionnaireTitle, so the question names the item's fieldset for assistive technology

a11y.by: questionnaire.test.tsx asserts the title renders as a LEGEND inside the current item's fieldset

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: The questionnaire engine's render prop takes an element or a function of the title's state (an empty state object for this part), so its type is a union of a React element and a callback; the compiler emits one JSON type per property, so nothing is asserted.

bad.title: A heading in place of the title
bad.why: A heading does not name the fieldset, so the choices are announced without the question they answer.

render.description: TS: RenderProp<RenderState> | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies. The questionnaire engine's render prop takes an element or a function of the title's state (an empty state object for this part), so its type is a union of a React element and a callback; the compiler emits one JSON type per property, so nothing is asserted.
